requirements.requirement: Restore /srv/inventory/data/config.json on node1 from the latest backup in /var/backups/inventory.
requirements.summary: The directory contained one backup, inventory-20260901.tar.gz. Its config.json was validated, restored, and verified byte-for-byte against the archive with SHA-256 1448a7478898f5e730573e8b09c55f4fecb9df2b5d9d1d8533adb09374316c7e.

requirements.requirement: Preserve all other current inventory files while restoring config.json.
requirements.summary: Before restoration, current.txt was the only other inventory file. It remained present with the same SHA-256 before restoration, afterward, and after restart; the final inventory still contained exactly config.json and current.txt.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory restart protocol is also complete: node1 was healthy before restart, acknowledged the restart, changed boot ID from 54bd1c3e-3a1b-4913-841b-88512119e096 to cc8bd39b-dfa8-4d8c-9a14-875c5a25eedb, and recovered with services and inventory data intact. The fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: Requirement restore_latest_backup cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-restore-data

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The restore command's temporary directory, extraction, metadata adjustment, and atomic replacement directly served the task and left no temporary artifact. The only other state-changing action was the required node-restart protocol; its transient reboot unit did not remain after reboot. Final observations show no failed units, unchanged socket exposure apart from expected new process IDs, and healthy package state.
